column1: # Game profile of Batman: Arkham Knight, update 1.0.5 (v327680; the base game is a 7 MB stub), SDK 14.3.0: Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 on NVN, Wwise on an AudioOut, CRI Sofdec movies,
# Scaleform menus. Generated by scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py (dm/games/profile_guess.py), then brought up on the Mac to its menus; the note (README.md) says what each key is for.
# The profile ships no shader tables: the NSP script makes them from the game files, in a profile derived from this one beside the build (derive_profile)
# The NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource (virtual address memory) and main never sets a heap. Its allocator would reserve 37 GB of address space (main+0x192fe50: 74 pools of 512 MB)
# and 1 GB more (main+0x192eee8); patches.py skips its construction and the host's allocator takes its place (hle_uemalloc.c). The game then maps one page of the alias region (the SDK's
# node area) and 14 MB of thread stacks, while the host heap outside the block holds 2.25 GB in gameplay: a 2 GB block (the alias region still fits the SDK's 1 GB node area) leaves the
# address space to the heap. Engage's 5 GB block ran out of address space on an iPad at 1.8 GB of heap
# the NPDM declares 32 MB of system resource
# Unreal Engine 3 writes its textures into their pools from the CPU after creating them, with no NVN flush (Batman: Arkham Asylum; profile_guess.py sets both for loose UE3 packages)
# The launchers' Render scale, Anti-aliasing and Texture filtering set the engine's own settings in its coalesced ini (hle_ue3ini.c): the Switch port locks the 3D scene to 75 % of the
# screen, leaves its SMAA off and filters 4×; its textures stay at the Switch's 256-pixel cap (the cook has nothing larger)
# 30 fps on the Switch only through the window's present interval 2: the engine's own limit is 62 (UGameEngine::GetMaxTickRate, main+0x1283dd4, returns MaxSmoothedFrameRate
# from [Engine.Engine] while the vsync flag main+0x5117244 is set), and the game steps by the time that really passed (GUseFixedTimeStep, main+0x483f800, is 0), so
# present_interval display gives 60 fps with the game clock at real time
